rounds.response: When you arrive, go through security, check in at the clerk’s window or courtroom clerk to confirm you’re in Department 12, sign any calendar sheet, and wait outside the courtroom until called. Bring copies of anything you’ve already filed (complaint/answer, your Case Management Statement if you filed one) and a short written summary of your position to hand to the clerk or judge if requested. In court the judge will ask both sides for a brief statement of the case, outstanding issues, discovery needs, ADR preference, and proposed schedule, then usually enter a scheduling order or set a follow‑up date. If you don’t have every document the judge might ask for, state that honestly, offer to provide missing items by a date the court sets, and expect the judge to either accept oral explanation, set deadlines for production, or continue the CMC; repeated failure to produce required documents can lead to sanctions, but routine gaps are typically resolved by scheduling orders. For specific form names, filing locations, or consequences that depend on local rules, ask the clerk or the court’s self‑help center or consult an attorney.

rounds.response: Many courts treat a missing separate Case Management Statement as a fixable procedural lapse—judges will often take a short oral statement at the CMC and then give you a deadline to file the required form—however practices vary so don’t assume that will always happen. Bring printed copies of your complaint and the email exhibits and hand a short written summary or the CMS to the courtroom clerk or the judge when called so the record shows you attempted to comply. Before you leave, ask the clerk how and when the court will issue the minute order (some courts post it to the online docket within hours or days; others will give or stamp a paper copy on request) and write down any dates the judge announces. Finally, confirm any deadlines on the record, file and serve any ordered documents by those dates, and contact the clerk or the court’s self‑help center immediately if the posted minute order or online docket differs from what was announced.
